chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from the one who mentioned him, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a sale in which there is measurement by volume or weight, he measures it out, and then takes it back in the same manner as it is in it. He said, 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy and immediately sell back measured goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of repurchasing goods that have already been measured or weighed, clarifying that such transactions are free from *gharar* (uncertainty) provided the condition of the goods remains unchanged. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between permissible commercial flexibility and prohibited ambiguity in sales contracts involving bulk commodities. The Imam’s concise verdict underscores the principle that prior measurement does not invalidate a subsequent sale of the same item under identical terms.
